newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta's drinks firm profits down.
newsitem.headline: Malta's drinks firm profits down.

text.p: Maltese soft drinks maker Simonds Farsons Cisk has announced pre-tax profits of Lm158,000 ($439,240) for the six-month period ending July 31 compared with Lm300,000 in the same period last year.

The company said turnover had "marginally increased" to Lm8.68 million from Lm8.5 million, but profitability was hit by "an enforced reduction in the price of Farsons beers as a result of an official price order", as well as a downturn in the hotel, restaurant and pub markets for beers and soft drinks.

"Another factor, which left its mark on the group's profitability during this period, was the substantial one-time losses incurred through heavy start-up costs for the fast food business," the group said.
Farsons has the Malta franchise for Burger King and Pizza Hut.

"This diversification of business is important for the future profitability of the group, which is confident that, with time, the fast food business will contribute satisfactory returns on investments."

"We are confident that we have a set of strategies to respond effectively to the fast changing business environment, although the trend of our profits for the current year is not likely to change," said the group's chief executive Louis Farrugia.
"However, we do expect to maintain last year's level of dividends."
Farsons is the only non-financial company listed on the Malta Stock Exchange.
